info.title: LCARS API
info.summary: LCARS for home: the HTTP side of the LCARS home display API.
info.description:
The LCARS home display API is served primarily over **NATS**, with protobuf message bodies. This reference covers the HTTP server that runs alongside it: a health check, these docs, and JSON versions of the NATS endpoints for debugging and simple clients.

## NATS API

Devices connect to the NATS server lcars-api runs (port `4222` by default) or to the one it is configured to use. Message bodies are protobuf messages defined in [`proto/lcars/v1`](https://github.com/asilluron/lcars-api/tree/main/proto/lcars/v1); generated Rust (prost) types are in the `lcars-proto` crate in [`rust/`](https://github.com/asilluron/lcars-api/tree/main/rust).

| Subject | Kind | Messages | HTTP equivalent |
|---------|------|----------|-----------------|
| `lcars.calendar.get` | request/reply | `GetCalendarRequest` → `GetCalendarResponse` | [`GET /calendar`](#operation/getCalendar) |
| `lcars.calendar.updated` | event | `CalendarUpdated`, published when the `.ics` files change | none |
| `lcars.cameras.list` | request/reply | `ListCamerasRequest` → `ListCamerasResponse` | [`GET /cameras`](#operation/listCameras) |
| `lcars.training.put` | request/reply | `PutTrainingAudioRequest` → `PutTrainingAudioResponse`. Appends 16 kHz mono PCM to an hourly WAV file in `training.dir`. No HTTP equivalent | none |

NATS error replies have an empty body and the headers `Nats-Service-Error-Code` (the same status code the HTTP endpoint would return) and `Nats-Service-Error` (the message). The service is named `lcars`, so it also answers `$SRV.PING.lcars`, `$SRV.INFO.lcars` and `$SRV.STATS.lcars`.

This reference is generated from the OpenAPI document the server itself serves at [`/openapi.json`](/openapi.json), and the version shown above is the version of the running build.

## Conventions

- **Encoding.** Request and response bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`) unless an operation says otherwise.
- **`HEAD`.** Every `GET` operation also answers `HEAD`, with the same status and headers and no body.
- **Authentication.** See [Authentication](#section/Authentication) below.
- **Dates and times.** Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`. Timestamps are [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339) with the UTC offset of the server's timezone, e.g. `2026-10-20T09:00:00-04:00`.
- **Versioning.** Paths are not versioned yet. The build version is reported by [`GET /healthz`](#operation/getHealth).

## Authentication

Authentication is on when the server is configured with a Supabase project (`supabase.url` and `supabase.secret_key`), and off otherwise, in which case anyone who can reach the server can use the API.

When it is on:

- **Devices** use a *device token*, made on the [admin page](/admin/): a username such as `dev_7f3k2m9q4x8w` and a secret password. Over HTTP, send them as [Basic auth](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7617) on the device endpoints (marked *deviceToken* below). Over NATS, connect to the embedded server with them as the user and password, e.g. `nats://dev_7f3k2m9q4x8w:<secret>@<host>:4222`; devices may then only send requests to the API's request subjects and subscribe to its event subjects. Revoking a token takes effect immediately and closes the NATS connections using it. (Tokens are not checked when lcars-api connects to an external NATS server with `nats.url`; secure that server separately.)
- **Admins** sign in on the admin page with an email and password. Admin accounts are Supabase Auth users, created by the operator (sign-ups are disabled). The admin API takes the access token from [`POST /admin/api/session`](#operation/createAdminSession) as a Bearer token.
- `/healthz`, `/openapi.json`, `/docs` and the admin page itself are always open.

There is no TLS: use the API only on a trusted network, or put it behind a reverse proxy that adds TLS.

## Errors

Errors raised by an operation have a JSON body with a single `error` field:

```json
{"error": "Internal Server Error"}
```

Unexpected failures, including panics, are logged on the server and returned as a `500` with a generic message, so internal details never reach the client.

Routing errors come from the router before any operation runs, and have a **plain-text** body:

| Status | When | Body |
|--------|------|------|
| `404` | No route matches the path. | `404 page not found` |
| `405` | The path exists, but not for this method. The `Allow` header lists the methods that are, e.g. `Allow: GET, HEAD`. | `Method Not Allowed` |

## Timeouts

The server closes connections that are slow to send headers (5 s) or a request (15 s), and responses that take longer than 15 s to write. A live camera stream ([`GET /cameras/{sn}/stream`](#operation/getCameraStream)) is the exception: it stays open until the client closes it. Idle keep-alive connections are closed after 60 s. On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT` it stops accepting new connections and waits for in-flight requests to finish before exiting.

tags.description: Process health, build information and NATS connection state.

tags.name: Calendar
tags.description:
Events read from `.ics` files on the host.

The server reads every `.ics` file under the directory set by `calendar.dir` in the config file (or `LCARS_CALENDAR_DIR`), including subdirectories, and re-reads it every `calendar.refresh_interval` (default one hour). Recurring events are expanded, including exceptions (`EXDATE`) and edited or cancelled occurrences (`RECURRENCE-ID`). A file that can't be parsed is skipped and logged on the server; the rest are still served.

Each event belongs to a calendar, named by the file's `X-WR-CALNAME` if set, otherwise by the top-level subdirectory the file is in, otherwise by the file name without `.ics`. So both `calendars/family.ics` and `calendars/family/*.ics` give a calendar named `family`.

tags.name: Admin
tags.description:
The admin page, and the API it uses to manage device tokens. Enabled only when Supabase is configured; otherwise every admin API operation answers `503`.

A device token's secret is returned once, when the token is created, and never stored: only a SHA-256 hash of it is. If it is lost, revoke the token and create a new one.

tags.name: Cameras
tags.description:
Cameras from the Eufy proxy named by `eufy.url` (`LCARS_EUFY_URL`). When that is unset, every camera operation answers `503`.

`GET /cameras` is the same catalog as `lcars.cameras.list`. `stream_path` and `snapshot_path` are paths on this server. The live video is Annex-B bytes and is not sent over NATS. Closing the stream response stops that viewer. A missing snapshot is `404` and does not wake the camera.

get.description: Reports that the process is up, along with the build version and the state of the NATS connection the API is served on. Answers `503` while that connection is down (for example, while an external NATS server is restarting); lcars-api reconnects on its own. It does no other work, so it is cheap to call often.

200.description: The server is up and connected to NATS.

503.description: The server is up, but its NATS connection is down, so NATS clients can't reach it.

get.description:
Returns the events in a range of days, grouped by day, ready to draw as an agenda or week view. Every day in the range is present, in order, even if it has no events.

Dates and times are in the server's timezone (`timezone` in the config file, or the host's), which the response reports. An event that spans several days appears on each of them. Within a day, all-day events come first, then timed events by start time.

Events are read from disk periodically, not on each request; `updated_at` says when they were last read.

The same data is available over NATS as a protobuf `GetCalendarResponse`, by sending a `GetCalendarRequest` on `lcars.calendar.get`. Subscribe to `lcars.calendar.updated` to learn when to fetch it again.

When authentication is on, this needs a device token (Basic auth).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day to list, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to today in the server's timezone.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Number of days to list, starting with `from`.

example.error: invalid "days": want a whole number from 1 to 62
calendar is not configured: set calendar.dir in the config file

get.description: The cameras the configured proxy currently reports, in the proxy's order. `stream_path` and `snapshot_path` are paths on this server. An empty `cameras` array means the proxy is up and has no devices.

503.description: Cameras are not configured, or the camera proxy could not be reached.

example.error: cameras are not configured: set eufy.url in the config file

get.description: Annex-B video for the camera (`video/octet-stream`). The response stays open until the client closes it, which stops that viewer on the proxy. It is not limited by the 15 second write timeout. A failure before the first byte is a JSON error. After the stream has started, a failure closes the connection.

parameters.name: sn
parameters.description: Camera serial: 1 to 32 letters or digits.

200.description: The live video. Read until you close the response.

400.description: The serial is not 1 to 32 letters or digits.

404.description: The proxy has no camera with that serial.

503.description: Cameras are not configured, or the camera proxy could not be reached.

get.description: The latest JPEG the proxy has stored for this camera. A miss is `404` and does not wake the camera.

parameters.name: sn
parameters.description: Camera serial: 1 to 32 letters or digits.

400.description: The serial is not 1 to 32 letters or digits.

404.description: No stored snapshot for that camera.

503.description: Cameras are not configured, or the camera proxy could not be reached.

get.description: Returns this OpenAPI 3.1 document, with `info.version` set to the version of the running build. Import it into an API client, or generate a typed client from it.

Returns the HTML page you are reading: a [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc) rendering of [`/openapi.json`](#operation/getOpenAPI). The page loads Redoc from a CDN, pinned to one version and checked with Subresource Integrity, so the browser viewing it needs internet access.

Returns the admin page, a single-page app for managing device tokens (sign in, create, list and revoke). Its scripts and styles are served from `/admin/assets/`. `GET /admin` redirects here.

The page is built into the binary by `make admin-ui` (and in the Docker image). A binary built without it answers `503` with a plain-text note.

503.description: The admin page was not built into this binary.

post.description: Signs an admin in with their Supabase Auth email and password, and returns an access token for the other admin operations. Supabase Auth limits how often sign-in can be attempted.

401.description: The email or password is wrong.

429.description: Too many sign-in attempts. Try again later.

example.error: too many sign-in attempts; try again later

get.description: Lists every device token, oldest first. Secrets are never included.

post.description: Creates a device token and returns it with its secret. The secret is not stored and cannot be retrieved again. The token works immediately, over HTTP and NATS.

201.description: The new token, with its secret.

delete.description: Deletes a device token. It stops working immediately, and NATS connections using it are closed.

404.description: There is no token with this ID.

name.description: Name from the camera account. May be empty.

stream_path.description: Path of the live Annex-B video on this server.

snapshot_path.description: Path of the latest stored JPEG on this server.

status.description: `ok` if the server is fully working; `unavailable` if its NATS connection is down.

version.description: Build version: the release tag (or `git describe` output) the binary was built from, or `(devel)` for an unversioned local build.

nats.description: State of the NATS connection the API is served on.

error.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

timezone.description: IANA name of the timezone all dates and times are in, or `Local` if the host's zone has no known name.

updated_at.description: When the `.ics` files were last read successfully.

days.description: One entry per day from `from` to `to`, in order.

today.description: Whether this day is today in the server's timezone.

events.description: Events overlapping this day: all-day events first, then by start time. Empty if there are none.

id.description: Identifies this occurrence: the event's `UID`, a slash, and its start time in UTC. Each occurrence of a recurring event has its own ID, and a multi-day event has the same ID on every day.

title.description: The event's `SUMMARY`. Empty if it has none.

calendar.description: Name of the calendar the event is from. See the Calendar section above for how it is chosen.

location.description: The event's `LOCATION`. Empty if it has none.

all_day.description: Whether this is an all-day event. All-day events have no times: `start` and `end` are midnights, and `start_time` and `end_time` are null.

end.description: When the occurrence ends (exclusive). For an all-day event on one day, this is midnight at the start of the next day.

start_time.description: Start time as `HH:MM` (24-hour), if a timed event starts on this day; null otherwise. Use it as the display label without parsing `start`.

end_time.description: End time as `HH:MM` (24-hour), if a timed event ends on this day; null otherwise. An event ending exactly at midnight shows `24:00` on the day before.

access_token.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` to the other admin operations.

id.description: The token's ID, which is also its username.

secret.description: The token's password: 43 base64url characters. Returned only here; store it on the device now.

name.description: A label for the device. Leading and trailing spaces are removed.

InternalError.description: The server failed unexpectedly. Details are logged on the server, not returned.

Unauthorized.description: No valid device token was sent (only when authentication is on). The `WWW-Authenticate` header asks for Basic auth.

example.error: a device token is required: send its username and password as HTTP Basic auth

AdminUnauthorized.description: No access token was sent, or it is invalid or expired. Sign in again.

example.error: your session has expired; sign in again

AdminUnavailable.description: The admin API is disabled because Supabase is not configured, or Supabase could not be reached (details are logged on the server).

example.error: the admin API is disabled: set supabase.url and supabase.secret_key in the config file

BadRequest.description: The request body is not valid JSON, has unknown fields, or has invalid values.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The request body is not sent as `application/json`.

example.error: send a JSON body with Content-Type: application/json

deviceToken.description: A device token's username (e.g. `dev_7f3k2m9q4x8w`) and secret. Required only when Supabase is configured.

adminSession.description: An access token from `POST /admin/api/session`. It expires after an hour by default.
